[[File:SE-D-eriaduoperative.gif|thumb|right|200px|[[Eriadu Operative]], Dark Side.]]
'''Operatives''' are a cycle of unrestricted [[Alien]] characters in [[Special Edition]]. Each title is tied to one planet. While at a matching site, an Operative adds 1 to Force drains there. It gains power or forfeit, and may deploy one site to that planet from Reserve Deck once during each of your deploy phases.<ref name="eriadu">[[Eriadu Operative]]</ref><ref name="alderaan">[[Alderaan Operative]]</ref>

[[Imperial Occupation / Imperial Control]] (Dark) and [[Local Uprising / Liberation]] (Light) flip and pay off around matching Operatives on a Renegade planet.<ref name="io">[[Imperial Occupation / Imperial Control]]</ref>

== 1998 World Championship ==

[[Special Edition]] was legal at the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]] before the public street date. Each of the 56 finalists received a complete set to build from.<ref name="insider43">Ryan Morris, "The Thrill of Victory", ''Star Wars Insider'' #43, pp. 64–65. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/starwarsinsider_1_to_153_plus_specials Star Wars Insider Magazines (1 to 153 + Specials)], Internet Archive. Facebook photographs, Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012404/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p64.html Internet Archive] (p. 64); [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016012452/https://swccg.com/snapshots/facebook/insider-1998-worlds-p65.html Internet Archive] (p. 65)</ref> [[Trandosite]] later called the weekend the Operative Worlds. Matching Operatives defined Saturday. [[Evan Ferguson]] finished 14th, the highest finisher who did not play them.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]].</ref>

[[Matt Potter]] won with 20 [[Eriadu Operative]] under Imperial Occupation (day-one Dark) and 20 [[Alderaan Operative]] under Local Uprising. [[Michael Riboulet]] won game 1 of the final by 19 with Dark Operatives; Potter won game 2 by 28, also on Operatives.<ref name="trando" />

[[Chuck Kallenbach]] wrote that Operatives were added late with little playtesting, and that Japanese testers asked for more copies before Virginia Beach. Players traded through the night for matching copies. [[Radio Free Decipher]] Broadcast 2 (11 December 1998) discussed a provisional ruling to errata rather than ban them after they became a negative play experience.<ref name="ck-worst">[https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ It was the Worst of Times. Period.], Chuck Kallenbach, i quote myself (28 February 2007). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210719164120/https://iquotemyself.wordpress.com/2007/02/28/it-was-the-worst-of-times-period/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="rfd2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w2Ao759YJlk&t=600s Radio Free Decipher Broadcast 2], Player's Council / Decipher (11 December 1998), 10:00–19:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-w2Ao759YJlk Internet Archive].</ref>

After the event Decipher issued errata that hit [[Spaceport Speeders]], then Operatives, [[Floating Refinery]], and [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]].<ref name="trando" /> Trandosite wrote that 1998 created more errata than Decipher had given out before.<ref name="trando" />

== Titles ==

Light Side titles include [[Alderaan Operative]], [[Anoat Operative]], [[Bothawui Operative]], [[Clak'dor VII Operative]], [[Corellia Operative]], [[Corulag Operative]], [[Dantooine Operative]], [[Kashyyyk Operative]], [[Kiffex Operative]], [[Kirdo III Operative]], [[Nal Hutta Operative]], [[Ord Mantell Operative]], [[Raithal Operative]], [[Ralltiir Operative]], and [[Tibrin Operative]].

Dark Side titles include [[Eriadu Operative]], [[Anoat Operative (Dark)|Anoat Operative]], [[Kashyyyk Operative (Dark)|Kashyyyk Operative]], [[Kessel Operative]], and [[Kiffex Operative (Dark)|Kiffex Operative]].
